title: Adaptive release velocity allocator for cycle-level staffing and scope
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight product-facing allocator that recommends per-cycle release velocity bands (low/medium/high) and suggested staffing buffers. The goal is to give PMs an actionable, data-driven starting point for scope cuts and staff shadowing decisions during planning. The allocator uses recent cycle throughput, role availability, known dependencies, and OKR risk to output: (1) a recommended velocity band, (2) minimum staffing cushion per role, and (3) a ranked set of candidate scope cuts categorized by risk and customer impact. This ticket delivers the UI wireframe, decision heuristics, integration points with the capacity dashboard, and a 2-week prototype for the next planning cycle.
comments: 2026-01-12 - Kickoff: aligned with Eng and Design on inputs: throughput histogram, role-level availability, unblock probability. Agreed success metric: reduce planning iteration time by 25% and surface 3 defendable scope cuts per cycle.

2026-01-18 - Design review: initial wireframes look good. Design suggests inline affordances for marking scope as 'surgical' vs 'defer' to bias automated ranking. Action: Design to supply microcopy and empty-state behavior by 1/22.

2026-01-25 - Eng scoping: ENG team flagged data freshness issue for role availability (current source is HR spreadsheet). Trade-off: ship prototype using a heuristically derived availability estimate, with Eng ticket to replace with API in sprint 2 (ENG-1842).

2026-01-28 - PM decision: bifurcate deliverable into an exploratory 'playbook' mode (read-only recommendations) and an eventual 'apply' mode (creates staffing requests and scope tags). Prototype will be read-only to reduce risk and speed feedback loops.

2026-02-04 - Prototype demo: ran allocator against last three cycles. Recommendation aligned with historical triage in 8/10 cases; flagged one false-positive where a customer-facing bug required re-prioritization. Outcome: add a manual 'override' note field and require a short rationale when overriding recommendations.

2026-02-10 - Design/PM feedback: reorder scope cut ranking to surface customer-impacted items first rather than size-first. Also request explicit link-outs to recent user incidents and support tickets to justify impact scores. Action: add 'evidence' links to ranking algorithm inputs.

2026-02-14 - Status update: prototype built (read-only) and wired to a synthetic dataset; user testing scheduled for 2026-02-20 with three PMs and two engineering managers. Next step: collect qualitative feedback and iterate prioritization heuristics.

Follow-ups: (a) ENG to implement availability API (ENG-1842), (b) Data to expose a tokenized incidents feed for evidence links, (c) Design to finalize microcopy and empty states, (d) PM to prepare acceptance criteria for rollout to pilot squads.
decisions: Prototype will be read-only (playbook mode) for first delivery to reduce operations risk.
Ranking heuristic will prioritize customer-impact evidence over raw effort estimate by default.
Use heuristic role-availability in prototype; swap to ENG availability API in sprint 2 (dependency ENG-1842).
next_steps: Complete user tests 2026-02-20 and capture change requests.
Implement evidence link ingestion (incidents/support) as input to ranking algorithm.
Create acceptance criteria for 'apply' mode and estimate effort for automation of staffing requests.
Coordinate with Data and Eng to wire production signals for cycle throughput and role availability.
